Description: I11 stands Violated (unrecorded SECURITY DEFINER bypass) and the P3-I11 conflict is unresolved. If Phase 4 binds any gate to the I11 verification before C6 closes, GD-2 forbids it (Violated or Suspended rule may not bind a gate), producing an illegal gate or a false approval.
Mitigation: Commit a dated ADR-board plan (ADR-003+) that records the I11 exception in R9 AND resolves the P3-I11 conflict with a precedence rule; keep the Phase 4 prohibition in force until the later architectural review confirms C6 closure.

Description: The I11 exception could be recorded as a bare R9 row (no ADR) or with an empty/unresolved authority field. R9/Spec-Exception require an ADR or authority; object-model §2.2 requires Exception to reference an ADR or authority; ADR-INDEX PQ-2 requires a Formal ADR. A bare row would not satisfy PQ-2 and would keep C6 open while appearing closed.
Mitigation: Require ADR-003+ (registered in ADR-INDEX, ADR-001 §2.1 series mechanics) as the only acceptable closing instrument; add a governance test asserting EXCEPTIONS contains exactly one Recorded entry targeting I11 with non-empty ADR authority, scope, and expiry.

Description: The P3-I11 conflict (RULE 12's two mandated homes: single authoritative aggregate model vs RLS sole access-control) has no precedence/reconciliation rule. An exception governs a deviation, not a contradiction between two frozen rules, so the conflict cannot be closed by an exception alone; a Suspended I11 still cannot bind a gate.
Mitigation: Amending ADR that reconciles the two homes (model home + RLS enforcement expression) and states the precedence between P3/I5 and I11 for access-control matrices; register a precedence-rule test (C.4).
Owner: D6 (Decision & Exception) / ADR board / D1 (Constitutional Definition)

Description: I11 is rated Ready (enforcement-architecture §6.1) because a bypass-detection verification is specifiable. An implementer could mistake Ready for permission to bind a gate, or bind the I11 verification while the exception is in force (Suspended).
Mitigation: Treat readiness as specifiability, not authorization; assert via a GD-2 test that no GATE_ELEMENT_ASSIGNMENT binds the I11 verification while I11 is Suspended/Violated, and that binding appears only after exception record + conflict ADR exist.

Description: While resolving C6, an implementer could modify frozen constitutional text (ADR-002 §3/§5, constitutional object-model/enforcement-architecture) outside the formal ADR process, violating Governance Freeze §3/§4 and the No-Change Boundary.
Mitigation: Route every text change through the amending ADR; keep the No-Change Boundary (documentation only) explicit; confirm zero changes to runtime code, SQL, seeds, registries, specifications, relationship models, APIs, commits, and tags as part of this analysis.

Description: EC8 audit chain is ambiguous at the constitutional-source level: object-model §2.3 and enforcement-architecture §2/§3 state Candidate A (Decision->Evidence->Constraint->Rule), while object-model §4 implies Candidate B (Decision->Gate->Verification->Evidence->Constraint->Rule). If the engine audit is built before the board selects, it may audit the wrong chain and produce false traceability failures or false approvals.
Mitigation: ADR board selects the canonical EC8 chain via formal ADR (ADR-INDEX PQ-1) before any engine audit work; record the other candidate as a projection; update MODEL-TRACEABILITY, MODEL-DECISION-PROVENANCE, decision.specification tracesTo, and the Phase-3 reports accordingly.

Description: Two 'EC8' referents exist: the exit-criterion EC8 (6 document-level traceability chains, architecture-transition-plan §9/AEM §2.4) and the object-level EC8 audit chain (object-model §2.3). Conflating them could cause the engine to merge the 6-chain re-verification with the decision-trace audit, or to skip the document-level re-verification entirely.
Mitigation: Record the two-referent distinction in the PQ-1 ADR; keep the document-level 6-chain re-verification as a separate EC8 verification scope the engine must implement; do not silently merge.

Description: If the board selects Candidate B, closing PQ-1 requires amending frozen text (object-model §2.3, enforcement-architecture §2/§3 Traceability definition, and the Phase-3 recorded chain). If the amendment is skipped and B is silently adopted, the recorded chain, reports, and provenance artifacts diverge from the constitution.
Mitigation: If B is selected, amend the frozen documents via formal ADR as part of the PQ-1 decision; if A is selected, no text change but record a confirmatory ADR plus the projection; always update the traceability/dependency-graph/object-relationship reports.

Description: Candidate B's audit chain requires edges records/produces, requires, evaluates, examines, constrained-by in the backward direction. If the chain is selected but DEPENDENCY_EDGE_DIRECTIONS or RELATIONSHIP_KINDS ranges are not updated for the new traversal, the engine could traverse links in the wrong direction.
Mitigation: Pin TRACEABILITY_CHAIN to the selected chain in the test suite; assert all audit-chain edges are within RELATIONSHIP_KINDS ranges and match DEPENDENCY_EDGE_DIRECTIONS; add an engine EC8-audit-shape scaffold test (no execution).

Description: The Phase-3 reports currently record Candidate A as the EC8 chain. If the board later selects B without updating phase3-dependency-graph-report §3, phase3-traceability-report §6, phase3-object-relationship-report, traceability-register, and registry-implementation-inventory, reports drift from the decision.
Mitigation: Update the listed reports (and, if B, the frozen documents) as part of the PQ-1 closing process; consider generating relationship reports from the vocabulary to prevent future drift.

Description: C6 and PQ-1 both require ADR-board decisions; neither may be substituted by a documentation note or an unapproved interpretation. If Phase 4 begins on the strength of this analysis alone (which is documentation only), the prohibitions (RUNTIME_ENFORCEMENT_PROHIBITED, SPECIFICATIONS_RUNTIME_PROHIBITED, RELATIONSHIPS_RUNTIME_PROHIBITED) and the Phase 4 prohibition are violated.
Mitigation: Treat the governance analysis as advisory; require the formal ADRs (ADR-003+) and the later architectural review confirming C1-C6 closure before any Phase-4 work; keep the No-Change Boundary.

Description: P7 circularity is a third known constitutional defect on its own ADR track. If it is pulled into the C6/PQ-1 decisions or ignored when provenance machinery is relied on, the decision scope expands or an unaddressed defect is silently carried into Phase 4.
Mitigation: Keep P7 on its own ADR-track item; record it as advisory (not gating Phase 4 under C6/PQ-1) but require its resolution before the provenance machinery it touches is relied on.

Description: After C6/PQ-1 close, new tests (R9 exception shape, GD-2 no-gate-binding invariant, I11 bypass-detection constraint, precedence rule, TRACEABILITY_CHAIN pinning, audit-chain edge assertions) are required. If added tests are absent or the closing ADR is registered without them, closure is not machine-verifiable.
Mitigation: Add the C.4 test set as a mandatory part of each closing decision; the later architectural review must confirm the tests are green before Phase 4.
